correctness.rationale: The Cayley identity C=2(I+sL)^-1-I and M-matrix positivity show all off-diagonals are positive for s>0 and sign loss is diagonal only. For paths, the reflecting heat-kernel diagonal equals q_{2r}(0)+q_{2r}(2i-1), and cycle kernel differences satisfy an irreducible cooperative tridiagonal ODE, making the center exactly minimal. Product semigroup and Laplace resolvent preserve minima. Cosine path spectrum supplies the finite central diagonal sum, strictly decreasing from 1 to 1/(mn)<1/2, hence unique threshold. Image-reflection terms show finite central Green > infinite square-lattice Green and convergence as both dimensions grow. Fourier integration gives G(s)=2K(4s/(1+4s))/(π(1+4s)), using elliptic modulus. The massive 2D axis Green has a unique Laplace saddle with exponent ξ=arcosh(1+1/(2s)); nearest images at ±n (odd) or n±1 (even) and exponential-moment tail control give the two explicit amplitudes with relative O(1/n). Independent direct 2D matrix inversion tested central min, entrywise threshold and sign changes for 5 different rectangles. This numerical test does not establish the all-grid limit or parity constants; those are supported by the analytic image and saddle calculation. Inspected source verification artifact also reports 2806 finite/numeric checks and high precision asymptotic ratios, not substitute proof.

final_claim: For every reflecting unit-weight rectangle P_m square P_n (m,n≥2), entrywise positivity of the Crank–Nicolson end-step holds iff s≤ a unique center-diagonal resolvent crossing. A two-dimensional square-lattice elliptic root s∞≈0.29409864 is the exact uniform bound, with parity-dependent leading square-grid corrections e^-ξn/sqrt(n).
